title: Work site pest fumigation preparation processes

lessons.title: Fumigation preparation on real sites
lessons.html:
Learning under close supervision

Fumigation preparation is high-risk work. In this module you assist registered fumigators on real jobs and gradually take responsibility for preparation tasks, always under direct supervision. Typical jobs include silo bin fumigations, bag stack fumigations in warehouses, container fumigations for export and structural fumigations of buildings.

Tasks you will practise

  • Walking the site to identify every gas escape route: conveyors, ducts, tunnels, drains, cable trenches and adjoining rooms.
  • Marking out exclusion zones and identifying nearby occupied areas.
  • Notifying occupants, workers and neighbours as the plan requires.
  • Evacuating people and animals and recording the occupancy check.
  • Locking out interconnected equipment with the site's authorised person.
  • Inspecting, repairing and laying gas-proof sheets; placing sand snakes.
  • Sealing hatches, slides, doors, vents and cracks.
  • Installing and labelling gas sampling lines.
  • Posting warning signs in suitable languages.
  • Checking respirators, canisters, gas monitors and first aid equipment.

Scenario

At a rural silo depot you help prepare bin 3 for phosphine fumigation. During the walk-through you notice that a conveyor gallery connects bin 3 to the weighbridge office, and that workers eat lunch in a container next to the bin. Your mentor praises the find: the conveyor is sealed and locked out, the lunch container is moved outside the exclusion zone, and monitoring is added at the weighbridge office. Spotting such connections is one of the most important skills you can develop.

lessons.title: Checklists, discipline and evidence
lessons.html:
Discipline saves lives

Fumigation teams rely on checklists because a single missed step can kill. Practise completing every checklist item honestly, never ticking a box for something not done.

Readiness checklist items

ItemConfirmed by
All escape routes sealed or isolatedTwo team members
Exclusion zone marked, signs postedTeam member and supervisor
Occupancy check completed and recordedTwo people, names and time
Sampling lines installed and labelledGas monitor operator
Respirators, canisters and monitors checkedEach user and supervisor
Emergency arrangements and label and SDS on siteSupervisor

Behaviour expected of you

  • Never enter a sealed or partly sealed structure without permission and the right protection.
  • Speak up immediately if you see something unsafe; any team member can stop the job.
  • Follow the supervisor's instructions exactly during preparation and application.
  • Handle fumigant products only when authorised and supervised.

Portfolio evidence

  • Copies of completed preparation and occupancy checklists you were part of.
  • Site sketches showing escape routes and exclusion zones.
  • Supervisor sign-off for each task performed.
  • Reflections on hazards you identified.

Key points

  • Work under direct supervision of a registered fumigator in this module.
  • Look for every gas escape route and occupied area near the fumigation.
  • Complete checklists honestly; never tick an item not done.
  • Any team member can and should stop unsafe work.
  • Keep signed checklists and site sketches as evidence.

quiz.question: In the silo depot scenario, what dangerous connection was found?

options.text: A conveyor gallery to the weighbridge office
A water pipe to the dam

quiz.question: What was done about the lunch container next to the bin?

options.text: It was sealed with workers inside
It was moved outside the exclusion zone

quiz.question: Who may handle fumigant products during this module?
How many people should complete the occupancy check?

options.text: Two, with names and time recorded

quiz.question: You notice an unsealed duct after application has been scheduled. What do you do?

options.text: Speak up immediately so the job can be stopped and corrected
Mention it in next week's report

quiz.question: It is acceptable to tick a checklist item you expect to finish later.
Which are possible gas escape routes to check? (select all that apply)
